title: Five Rescued Off Kiribati After Three Months Adrift in the Pacific
excerpt: Three adults and two children survived a 5,400-kilometre drift in a 20-foot skiff after a storm wrecked a one-hour island crossing in Micronesia; four companions are still missing.
body:
• Five people — three adults and two children — were rescued off Fanning Island in Kiribati on Sunday, November 1, after drifting in a 20-foot skiff for about three months.
  • The group of nine set out on July 30 on a one-hour crossing between the Micronesian islands of Murilo and Ruo and were caught in a storm.
  • A 10-day US Coast Guard search covering some 25,000 square nautical miles found no trace of the boat before it was called off on August 9.
  • The fate of the other four people aboard remains unknown; the survivors arrived severely dehydrated and malnourished and are receiving care.

Five people, including two children, have been rescued in Kiribati after drifting across the Pacific in a 20-foot skiff for roughly three months, the US Coast Guard in Guam confirmed on Tuesday. Villagers on Fanning Island, also known as Tabuaeran, spotted the boat off the island on Sunday and brought the survivors ashore, the Australian Broadcasting Corp. reported.

The five were among nine people who left Murilo island in the Federated States of Micronesia on July 30 for Ruo island, a crossing that normally takes about an hour. A storm caught the skiff during the trip and pushed it far out to sea. By the time it reached Fanning Island, the boat had drifted an estimated 5,400 kilometres (3,355 miles) east of Micronesia, according to the Associated Press.

A search that found nothing

The skiff was reported missing after it failed to return to Ruo on July 30. The US Coast Guard searched for 10 days, covering about 25,000 square nautical miles (85,700 square kilometres), without finding any sign of the vessel or the people aboard, and suspended the operation on August 9.

https://x.com/KTLA/status/2117591981459398675

In an email to the Associated Press, the Coast Guard called the rescue "incredible and wonderful news" and said the five were receiving care. Asked what had happened to the four people still missing, the Coast Guard said it was continuing to gather and confirm information.

Dehydrated, malnourished, but recovering

Nursing officer Paukin Tororo told the ABC that all five survivors arrived severely dehydrated and malnourished. They were put on intravenous drips and are recovering. The survivors have not yet spoken publicly about the ordeal and have asked for privacy, the broadcaster reported. A Kiribati lawmaker, Kaotitaake Rakoroa, said the group received medical attention and is in the care of a local pastor.

"Thanks be to God for his love and mercy that five of the nine people have been found. We continue to pray for their four companions."

— Alexander Narruhn, Governor of Chuuk State, Micronesia

The journey home

Alexander Narruhn, governor of Micronesia's Chuuk state, said in a statement on Sunday that he had asked the president of the Federated States of Micronesia to work with the Kiribati government to bring the survivors home. Talks between the two governments have begun, according to the governor.

What happened to the four missing passengers is still not known. Neither the Coast Guard nor Kiribati officials have said whether they are believed to have survived.
